01 — Who we are

More Than Just
Smart Home.

Here at Tall Tech, our mission goes beyond providing Smart Home & Business solutions. We specialise in creating personalised smart living experiences perfect for any home or budget. New construction or decades old, we can turn any home into a Smart Home.

Life gets busy — but when your home technology is connected into one simple-to-use system, it helps take away some of those daily little stresses. A true smart home makes your life more convenient and your home safer, more comfortable and easy to enjoy.

Through our comprehensive range of services & products, we ensure our clients stay ahead in the ever-changing technology landscape with the latest and most innovative products on the market, ensuring a future proof Smart Home.

"By leveraging innovative solutions, we streamline processes, automate tasks, and reduce the time spent on everyday challenges. This allows our clients to focus on what they love. Technology should work for you, not the other way around. We're dedicated to making life easier so our clients can reclaim their time and create lasting memories."

Smart Home Automation

Control4-powered systems that connect every device in your home into one seamless, intuitive experience.

Alarm, CCTV & Access

World-class security and access control solutions engineered to the highest standards of reliability.

Multi-Room Audio Visual

Cinema-grade AV experiences throughout the home, from poolside speakers to dedicated home theatres.

Networking & Wi-Fi

Enterprise-grade networking infrastructure ensuring flawless connectivity throughout every square metre.

Lighting Control

Philips Dynalite and smart lighting solutions that set the perfect mood for every room and occasion.

Brisbane & Noosa

Dedicated teams servicing two of Queensland's most vibrant and growing luxury residential markets.

02 — Points of culture

The Standards
We Set.

These are the values and aspirations that define how we work and who we are. Read each one. Understand it. Live it.

03 — Workplace policies

Rules of
the Game.

These are the non-negotiables. Every person at Talltech is expected to know them, follow them, and hold each other to them.

Conduct & Behaviour

Treat every colleague, client, contractor, and member of the public with respect and professionalism at all times — in person, in writing, on the phone, and online.

Be on time, every time. If you are going to be late or absent, call your manager directly — a text or email is not sufficient.

Follow all reasonable and lawful instructions from your manager. If you disagree with a direction, raise it through the right channels — do not simply ignore it.

No bullying, harassment, or discrimination of any kind. This applies on site, in vehicles, at events, and through any digital channel.

Do not engage in any illegal activity on company premises, client sites, or in company vehicles — including theft, possession of illegal substances, or carrying weapons.

Presentation & Client Standards

Wear your uniform consistently during work hours. Keep it clean and return it when you leave. On site: hi-vis, work pants, and steel-capped boots — no exceptions.

Greet clients by name. Listen actively. Respond promptly. Never swear or behave disrespectfully in front of a client — or in any context where you represent the brand.

Treat client property with care and respect at all times. You are a guest in their home or business.

Any media enquiry must be directed to the Operations Manager immediately. No employee may speak to the media without written director approval.

Vehicles & Travel

Only authorised staff may drive a company vehicle. You must hold a valid licence and provide it for management review on request.

Zero tolerance — never drive under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or any impairing substance. No handheld mobile phone use while driving.

All fines — traffic, speeding, and parking — are your personal and financial responsibility. The company will not pay or reimburse them.

Any incident or damage, no matter how minor, must be reported to management immediately with photos within 24 hours.

Personal toll charges are your responsibility and will be recovered via payroll each pay cycle. Work tolls (Mon–Fri 07:30–15:30) are covered by the company.

The fuel card is for fuel only — not food, drinks, or personal items. Personal trips exceeding 50km one-way require prior written approval.

Technology & Information

Use company devices and systems for work purposes only. Limited personal use is permitted but must not interfere with your work or create any security or legal risk.

Use unique, complex passwords stored only in an encrypted vault. Never share, write down, or hint at any password to anyone.

Report any lost or stolen device or suspected data breach to the Operations Manager immediately. Do not try to manage it yourself.

Do not post anything on social media that identifies, references, or reflects on Talltech, its clients, or its people in a misleading, offensive, confidential, or brand-damaging way — during or outside work hours.

Client and company information is confidential. Do not disclose project details, client names, pricing, or commercial information to anyone outside the business.

Money & Resources

Use company resources — time, equipment, vehicles, and consumables — only for legitimate work purposes. Waste and misuse are not acceptable.

Any cash discrepancy, petty cash anomaly, or unexplained payment variance must be reported to the Operations Manager immediately upon discovery.

Gifts received from clients or suppliers must be reported to the Operations Manager regardless of value and logged in the gifts register. When in doubt, do not accept.

Salaried employees receive Time Off In Lieu (TOIL) for overtime by default. Cash payment requires director approval. Hourly employees receive penalty rates per their applicable Award.

Secondary employment must be disclosed to the Operations Manager before commencing. You cannot perform work for another employer during Talltech working hours or on company premises.

Health, Safety & Wellbeing

Wear PPE whenever it is required. Do not alter or remove safety equipment. Comply with all safety signs, procedures, and site rules.

Zero tolerance for alcohol and drugs. Do not attend work under the influence of any substance. Alcohol is only permitted at approved company events.

Report every incident, injury, near-miss, or notifiable event immediately. Do not wait to see if it becomes a problem — reporting protects you and the team.

Keep work areas clean and tidy to prevent trip and slip hazards. Report faults or maintenance needs promptly — do not wait for the issue to worsen.

Do not use personal devices while driving, operating machinery, or working at height — or in any other situation where device use creates a safety risk.

Tolls

All vehicles have a Linkt tag. Work tolls are covered by the company. Personal tolls are recovered via payroll. Refer to the People & Culture Handbook for full classification detail.

Personal tolls appear on your payslip as "Personal Tolls" and are deducted in the first pay run of the following month.

If you think a toll has been classified incorrectly, you have 7 days from the payroll notice to dispute it — email payroll with the date, time, location, tag number, and vehicle driven.

Keep your tag fitted and in your assigned vehicle. The tag stays with the vehicle — not with you — and must be returned when you leave or change vehicles.

Personal Commutes & 50km Radius

Your paid day starts when you arrive at your designated Showroom (Brisbane or Noosa). Travel from home to the Showroom — or from home directly to a job site — is ordinary commuting and is personal time.

The 50km radius is measured from your designated Showroom — not from where you live. Jobs within 50km: your commute is personal. Jobs beyond 50km: working-away provisions apply and travel becomes paid work time.

Tolls on personal legs (home to Showroom, and home to/from any job within 50km) are personal and recovered via payroll. Tolls on business legs are covered by the company.

If you choose to leave earlier than required for personal reasons, that extra travel time is not paid work time and does not attract overtime — unless your manager has given prior written approval.

Personal use of a company vehicle exceeding 50km one-way requires prior written approval from the Operations Manager or a director. Approval is not guaranteed and is not a precedent for future requests.

Sexual Harassment & Bullying

Zero tolerance. Sexual harassment, bullying, and harassment of any kind are not tolerated under any circumstances — regardless of role, seniority, or length of service.

This policy applies everywhere — on site, in vehicles, at work events and social functions, through email, SMS, and social media, and outside the workplace where the conduct has a connection to work.

Sexual harassment includes unwelcome physical contact, sexually suggestive comments or jokes, displaying or sharing explicit material, persistent unwanted romantic attention, and any conduct of a sexual nature that would cause a reasonable person to feel offended, humiliated, or intimidated.

Bullying includes repeated unreasonable behaviour — verbal abuse, exclusion, overloading work, withholding information, or any behaviour that creates a risk to health and safety. A single incident may not be bullying, but it must not be ignored.

The standard that people walk past is the standard they accept. If you witness this behaviour, you have an obligation to report it — not stand by.

Report to your direct manager, the Operations Manager, or a director. No person will be disadvantaged for raising a genuine concern in good faith. External options include the Queensland Human Rights Commission (1300 130 670) and 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732).

Technician — Role Policies

Tools, Vehicles & Client Sites

Tool accountability: You are responsible for all tools and equipment assigned to you. Tools must be returned to the warehouse clean and in working condition. Lost or damaged tools must be reported immediately — not when they're needed next.

Client property: Treat every client home with absolute respect. No eating or drinking in client spaces without permission. Leave every site cleaner than you found it. If you damage something — tell your coordinator immediately. Do not hide it.

Daily vehicle check: Complete a vehicle check via the staff portal every day before driving. This protects you legally and ensures the fleet is roadworthy. Skipping it is not acceptable.

Site communication: Keep your coordinator updated throughout the day. If a job is running over, call ahead — never go silent on site. If you have a problem you can't solve, escalate early, not at 4:30pm.

Programmer — Role Policies

Code, Licensing & Client Systems

All code belongs to Talltech: Any programming, templates, driver code, or system designs you create during your employment are the intellectual property of Talltech. Do not copy, distribute, or reuse them outside the business.

Licensing compliance: Only use licensed software and authorised drivers. Do not install unlicensed plugins, cracked drivers, or grey-market firmware on any client or company system. This exposes the business to serious legal risk.

Remote access: All remote access to client systems must be logged in the project notes with date, time, and purpose. Never leave back-door access open on a client system after the engagement is complete.

Documentation: Every completed system must have up-to-date as-built documentation uploaded to the project folder before the job is marked complete. This is not optional — undocumented systems create service nightmares.

Sales — Role Policies

Client Relations, Quoting & Commitments

No verbal commitments on pricing or scope: You may never verbally commit to a price, discount, or scope of work without a written quote approved by Nico or a director. Verbal agreements made in good faith still bind the business — get it in writing first.

Gifts & entertainment: You may receive gifts, meals, or entertainment from suppliers and clients. Anything over nominal value must be disclosed to the Operations Manager and logged. You may not accept gifts that could influence your purchasing or referral decisions.

CRM discipline: All client interactions, quotes, follow-ups, and outcomes must be logged in the CRM the same day. The business makes decisions based on CRM data — incomplete records cost everyone.

Competitor conduct: Do not denigrate competitors or their products to clients. Sell on Talltech's merits. Negative comparisons reflect poorly on us, damage trust, and frequently backfire.

Admin / Office — Role Policies

Finance, Records & Supplier Management

Financial records: All financial records — invoices, purchase orders, receipts — must be accurate, filed promptly, and never altered after the fact. If you make an error, flag it to your manager and correct it through the proper process. Do not simply delete or overwrite.

Purchase authority: You may only raise purchase orders within your approved limit. Any purchase outside your approved limit must be authorised by the Operations Manager or a director before committing. A verbal "yes" is not a PO.

Supplier relationships: Treat all suppliers professionally. Do not negotiate outside your remit, make informal arrangements, or accept inducements that could compromise supplier objectivity. All supplier arrangements go through approved channels.

Staff data privacy: In your role, you may have access to sensitive employee information. This is strictly confidential. Do not discuss, share, or reference any personal information outside of its legitimate business purpose.

Project Manager — Role Policies

Scope, Variations & Team Management

Variations must be documented: Any work outside the original contract scope must be raised as a variation and approved in writing by the client before it is carried out. Do not instruct technicians to do out-of-scope work on a "we'll sort it later" basis.

Directing your team: Your instructions to technicians and programmers must be clear, achievable, and within their competency. If you assign a task beyond someone's skill level, you are responsible for ensuring they have the support they need to do it safely.

Budget & forecasting: Maintain your project budget tracker weekly. Flag any cost overruns to the Operations Manager as soon as you identify the risk — not after the fact. Cost surprises at practical completion are not acceptable.

Head contractor relationships: You are Talltech's representative on site. Your conduct with the head contractor reflects on the business. Be professional, proactive, and solutions-focused. Disputes must be escalated to Scott, not resolved unilaterally.

04 — Health & safety

Everyone
Goes Home Safe.

Working in homes and construction environments carries real hazards. Before you pick up a tool, you need to understand the basics — what a hazard is, what makes something notifiable, and how to plan work safely.

Your health and wellbeing at work matters. This section covers what Talltech expects of every employee — regardless of role — when it comes to workplace safety, reporting, and looking after yourself and your team.

Hazard

Anything with the potential to cause harm. Examples: exposed wiring, a wet floor, working at heights, heavy objects, chemical substances.

Risk

The likelihood and consequence of a hazard causing harm. A hazard always exists — risk is how probable it is that harm will actually occur, and how severe.

Incident

Any unplanned event that results in — or had the potential to result in — injury, illness, or property damage. This includes near-misses. All incidents must be reported.

Job Safety Analysis (JSA)
Complete before any non-routine or higher-risk task — submitted via the staff portal

A JSA breaks a job into steps, identifies the hazards in each step, and documents the controls you'll apply using the hierarchy of controls. It must be completed and on-site before work begins. Use it for any task that carries real risk — drilling, working at heights, running cable in confined spaces, or anything unfamiliar.

3

4

5

Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS)
Legally required for all high-risk construction work under the WHS Regulations

A SWMS is a formal written document required by law before commencing high-risk construction work. Unlike a JSA, a SWMS must be prepared in advance, kept on site at all times, and signed by every worker before they begin. If site conditions change, the SWMS must be reviewed before work continues.

High-Risk Work That Requires a SWMS
Work at heights >2m Energised electrical work Confined spaces Demolition work Excavation >1.5m deep Work near live traffic

Notifiable Incidents
Must be reported to Workplace Health & Safety Queensland (WHSQ) immediately
Death
The death of any person at the workplace, regardless of whether they are a worker or visitor.
Serious Injury or Illness
Amputation, serious head or eye injury, serious burns, loss of consciousness, spinal injury, or immediate hospitalisation.
Dangerous Incident
Uncontrolled escape of a hazardous substance, electric shock, collapse of a structure, explosion or fire — even if no one is hurt.
Call 000 for emergencies. Report notifiable incidents to WHSQ on 1300 362 128. Do not disturb the scene until authorised.

Hierarchy of Controls

Always work down this list — use the highest-level control that is reasonably practicable.

Most Effective
Least Effective
1
Elimination

Best
2
Substitution

3
Engineering Controls

4

Change the way people work — procedures, training, signage
5
PPE

Technician — Additional Requirements

On-Site & Physical Work Safety

Working at height: Any work above 1.8m requires a JSA, appropriate fall protection (harness or safety cage), and a spotter where practical. Do not improvise — use the correct rated ladder or scaffold.

Electrical safety: Always isolate and test before working on or near live circuits. Never assume a circuit is dead. Lock Out / Tag Out procedures must be followed. Inform the site supervisor before any isolation.

Confined spaces & roof cavities: Assess the space before entry — check for heat, chemical exposure, restricted egress, and ventilation. If in doubt, raise it with your coordinator before proceeding.

Manual handling: Lift with your legs, not your back. Use a trolley or ask for help with anything over 20kg. Equipment racks must always be moved with two people.

PPE minimum requirements: Steel-capped boots, safety glasses when drilling/cutting, gloves when handling cables, and hi-vis vest on active construction sites. Your coordinator will advise if additional PPE is required.

SWMS on construction sites: Before commencing work on any active construction site, you must have a completed and signed Safe Work Method Statement. Do not start without it.

Programmer — Additional Requirements

Programming & Lab Safety

Client site access: When on-site for commissioning, you still fall under the site's safety rules. Wear required PPE, sign in, and attend any site induction. Your programmer status does not exempt you from site requirements.

Rack and equipment handling: Racks weigh significantly — never attempt to move or rack-mount heavy equipment alone. Always team lift and use proper rail kits.

Screen & ergonomics: Extended programming sessions carry real ergonomic risk. Use a proper chair with lumbar support, take a 5-minute break from screen every hour, and adjust monitor height to eye level.

Client system access: Never access a client system remotely without explicit written or verbal approval from the client or project coordinator. Log all remote sessions with start/end time in the project notes.

Sales — Wellbeing & Work Health

Your Health & Wellbeing at Work

Right to disconnect: Under the Fair Work Act 2009, you have the right to refuse to monitor or respond to work communications outside your ordinary hours unless the refusal is unreasonable. Receiving a message does not obligate you to respond. If you choose to review messages out of hours, that is your choice — it does not set an expectation for others.

Psychosocial hazards: Excessive workload, unreasonable after-hours pressure, poor role clarity, and interpersonal conflict are all recognised psychosocial hazards under the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld). If you are experiencing any of these, raise it with your manager or the Operations Manager. These are safety matters, not personal ones.

Fatigue & driving: Sales roles involve significant time on the road. Do not drive if fatigued — fatigue impairment is comparable to alcohol impairment. If you are too tired to drive safely, stop. Never use a handheld device while driving. Zero tolerance applies to driving a company vehicle after any alcohol.

Alcohol at work functions: Responsible consumption is permitted at organisation-sanctioned functions. You are expected to arrange safe transport home. Being intoxicated at a work function may result in disciplinary action. Zero tolerance applies from the start of the next working day.

Reporting incidents: Any injury, near miss, or hazard — including those that occur while driving or at a client site — must be reported through the Talltech Staff Portal. Vehicle accidents must be reported to the Operations Manager by phone the same day, and via the portal within 24 hours.

Support: If you are struggling — with workload, a personal matter, or your mental health — speak with your manager or the Operations Manager. Your GP can also refer you to mental health services, some of which are accessible under a Medicare Mental Health Care Plan. Beyond Blue: 1300 22 4636. Lifeline: 13 11 14.

Admin / Office — Wellbeing & Work Health

Your Health & Wellbeing at Work

Right to disconnect: Under the Fair Work Act 2009, you have the right to refuse to monitor or respond to work communications outside your ordinary hours unless the refusal is unreasonable. Receiving a message does not create an obligation to respond. If you have concerns about after-hours pressure, raise them with the Operations Manager — unreasonable after-hours demands are a psychosocial hazard under the WHS Act.

Workstation & ergonomics: Set your chair so your feet are flat, elbows at 90°, and the top of the monitor at eye level. Take a short break from screen work every hour. If you develop any discomfort — neck, wrist, back — report it early. Do not push through RSI-type symptoms. Early intervention prevents long-term injury.

Alcohol & impairment (office standard): You must not attend the office in a state of impairment that affects your ability to perform your duties safely or professionally — whether from alcohol, drugs, or medication. If you are unsure whether you are fit to work, contact your manager before commencing. If a colleague appears impaired, raise it with the Operations Manager discreetly.

Emergency procedures: Know your evacuation plan and muster point. Know where the fire extinguishers, first aid kit, and defibrillator are located. If someone is injured, call 000 immediately if there is any risk to life. All incidents — including slips, trips, and near misses — must be reported via the Talltech Staff Portal the same day.

Psychosocial hazards: Workload, role ambiguity, interpersonal conflict, and excessive after-hours demands are all recognised psychosocial hazards under the WHS Act. If you are experiencing any of these, you are entitled to raise it. Speak with your manager or the Operations Manager. These are workplace safety issues, not personal weaknesses.

Support: Your GP can refer you to mental health and counselling services, some accessible under a Medicare Mental Health Care Plan. Beyond Blue: 1300 22 4636. Lifeline: 13 11 14. 1800RESPECT (family violence support): 1800 737 732.

Project Manager — Additional Requirements

Site Management & Team Safety

Your safety obligations: As PM, you are responsible for ensuring every Talltech worker on your site has completed the required SWMS/JSA before work commences. If documentation is incomplete, work stops until it is done.

Site inductions: Coordinate with the head contractor to ensure all Talltech personnel have completed the site-specific induction before their first day on site. This is your responsibility — not the technician's.

Incident reporting: If any incident or near-miss occurs on your site, you must report it to Scott same day. The incident report must be lodged in the staff portal within 24 hours, regardless of severity.

Subcontractors: Ensure any subcontractors working alongside Talltech have their own valid SWMS and public liability insurance in place before they set foot on site. Copies go in the project file.

Mental health of your team: If a team member shows signs of fatigue, stress, or is behaving unusually, raise it with Scott. Project pressure is never an excuse to ignore someone's wellbeing.

Rules of the Game — Knowledge Check

10 questions — 5 covering universal Talltech standards, and 5 specific to your role.

Conduct & BehaviourYou disagree with a direction given by your manager. What is the correct course of action under Talltech's conduct expectations?

Reporting AbsenceYou are going to be late to work. What does Talltech require you to do?

Gifts & Gifts RegisterA supplier drops off a gift basket at the office for you. What must you do?

Bullying & HarassmentYou witness a colleague being repeatedly spoken to aggressively by another team member. What does Talltech expect of you?

Secondary EmploymentYou have been offered casual work with another business on weekends. What must you do before accepting?

Technician — JSAYou are about to start a cable run through a roof cavity you have not worked in before. What must you do first?

Technician — Client PropertyWhile on site, you accidentally scratch a client's freshly painted wall. What should you do?

Technician — Electrical SafetyYou need to run a cable near what looks like an energised circuit. What must you do before proceeding?

Technician — Daily Vehicle CheckHow often must you complete a vehicle check through the staff portal?

Technician — ToolsA tool assigned to you goes missing on site. What is the correct action?

Programmer — IP OwnershipYou write a custom Control4 driver during your employment at Talltech. Who owns it?

Programmer — Remote AccessYou remotely log into a client system to fix a bug. What must you do?

Programmer — LicensingYou find a useful third-party driver online but it has no clear licence. What should you do?

Programmer — DocumentationYou finish commissioning a system. When must as-built documentation be uploaded to the project folder?

Programmer — On-Site PPEYou attend a client site for commissioning and the head contractor requires a hard hat and steel-caps. What applies?

Sales — Verbal CommitmentsA client verbally agrees to a scope change during a site meeting and asks you to confirm the price. What must you do?

Sales — CRMYou have a productive call with a prospect and agree on next steps. When should this be logged in the CRM?

Sales — Competitor ConductA client asks how Talltech compares to a competitor they have also spoken to. What is the right approach?

Sales — Solo VisitsYou have a residential site visit booked for 4pm in an area you have not been to before. What must you do beforehand?

Sales — Right to DisconnectIt is 9pm on a Sunday and you receive a non-urgent work message. Under the Right to Disconnect policy, what applies?

Admin — Purchase AuthorityYou need to order supplies urgently and the cost will exceed your approved limit. What do you do?

Admin — Financial RecordsYou notice a mistake in a financial record you entered earlier. What is the correct course of action?

Admin — Staff DataA colleague asks you about another employee's personal details you have access to through your role. What do you do?

Admin — Cash DiscrepancyYou notice a petty cash anomaly at the end of the day. What must you do?

Admin — Right to DisconnectYou send a work message to a colleague at 8pm on a weekday. What must you not create?

PM — VariationsThe client verbally asks for additional scope during a site visit. What must happen before any work begins?

PM — SWMS ResponsibilityYour technicians are due on site tomorrow but the SWMS has not been completed. What happens?

PM — Budget OverrunYou realise mid-project that costs are trending over budget. When must you raise this?

PM — SubcontractorsA subcontractor is ready to begin work on your site. What must be in place before they start?

PM — Dispute with Head ContractorThe head contractor makes a decision on site you strongly disagree with. What is the correct approach?
